topics.title: Photosynthesis mechanism (synthetic)
canonicalFacts: Light energy is captured by chlorophyll.
Carbon dioxide and water are inputs.
caveats: This is a simplified teaching model, not a full biochemical pathway.
topics.conceptPrompt: In your own words, explain how photosynthesis converts inputs into stored energy. Include what goes in, what comes out, and the role of light.
topics.transferPrompt: A closed terrarium has plants but no new air from outside. Using only the photosynthesis facts above, what gas would you expect to increase if the plants keep photosynthesizing, and why?

mustNotClaim: photosynthesis consumes oxygen as the only product

topics.title: Chemical energy in a simple battery model (synthetic)
canonicalFacts: During discharge, chemical energy converts to electrical energy.
Voltage is the electrical potential difference between terminals.
Capacity describes how much charge the battery can deliver.
caveats: This model ignores chemistry-specific side reactions and thermal losses.
topics.conceptPrompt: Explain how a battery provides usable energy. Cover what is stored, what is delivered, and what voltage vs capacity mean at a conceptual level.
topics.transferPrompt: Two batteries have the same voltage but one has twice the capacity. For the same device load, which lasts longer, and which fact justifies that?

topics.title: Recursion via factorial (synthetic)
canonicalFacts: Recursion solves a task using smaller versions of the same task.
A base case stops the recursion.
caveats: This illustrates recursion structure; it is not a claim about optimal algorithms.
topics.conceptPrompt: Explain recursion using factorial. Include the recursive relation, the base case, and compute factorial(4).
topics.transferPrompt: Using the same recursive idea, what is factorial(5)? Show the relation to factorial(4).

topics.title: Loop accumulation (synthetic)
canonicalFacts: A loop repeats a body while a condition holds.
An accumulator variable stores a running result.
When the loop ends, the accumulator holds the final result.
caveats: This is a conceptual model; language-specific loop syntax is omitted.
topics.conceptPrompt: Explain how a loop with an accumulator computes a running product of integers from 1 to n. State the role of the condition and the accumulator.
topics.transferPrompt: If the accumulator starts at 1 and multiplies by each integer from 1 to 4, what final value should it hold, and which fact justifies that?
